pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: You want to read all of `notes.txt` into memory and later write it back. Which `os` functions do you reach for, what types do they work with, and what must you do after every call?
expected_points: os.ReadFile returns ([]byte, error); os.WriteFile takes []byte plus permission bits like 0o644
convert between []byte and string as needed
check the error after every call — files fail for reasons the code cannot prevent
os.WriteFile replaces the whole file, it does not append

questions.prompt: What exactly does Go guarantee about a deferred call? If a function defers three `Close` calls, in what order do they run — and why is that order sensible?
expected_points: deferred calls run when the surrounding function returns, on every path: normal return, early return, even a panic
multiple defers run LIFO — last deferred, first executed
later-acquired resources may depend on earlier ones, so cleanup unwinds in reverse order of setup

questions.prompt: Sketch (in words or code) the loop that processes a file line by line, and name the step people most often forget.
expected_points: os.Open, check the error, defer f.Close()
bufio.NewScanner(f), then for scanner.Scan() { use scanner.Text() }
after the loop check scanner.Err() — Scan returns false for both EOF and a read failure, and only Err distinguishes them

questions.prompt: The package is called bufio — buffered I/O. What is being buffered, and why does it matter for speed?
expected_points: every read from a file is a system call to the OS, far slower than touching memory
bufio reads a large chunk per system call into a memory buffer and serves lines/bytes from it
without buffering, line-by-line or byte-by-byte reading would mean a huge number of system calls

questions.prompt: Your tracker's data file versus a multi-gigabyte server log: for each, whole-file read or streaming, and what is the reasoning?
expected_points: small file needed in full → os.ReadFile: simpler code, memory cost is fine
huge or unbounded file, sequential processing, or early exit → stream with bufio.Scanner: constant memory
the trade-off axis is memory footprint versus simplicity

questions.prompt: `defer f.Close()` ignoring the error is accepted when reading a file but frowned upon when writing one. Why the difference?
expected_points: on a write path the OS may only flush data at close time, so a failing Close can mean the data never reached disk
ignoring it loses data silently; check Close's error explicitly when writing
after a read there is nothing left to lose, so the deferred, unchecked Close is harmless

questions.prompt: Why must a missing file be detected with `errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist)` rather than `err == os.ErrNotExist`?
expected_points: os functions return a *PathError that wraps the sentinel, not the sentinel itself
errors.Is walks the wrap chain; == only compares the outermost value and fails
wrapping with %w keeps this inspection working while adding context
